txs.name: Transformer feeding MSB8
txs.notes: Specified 3,150 kVA, 11/0.415 kV Dyn11, TN-S. Rating is settled and does not wait for anything: the per-circuit demand factors give 4,172 kVA and the tightest coincidence band gives 6,015 kVA, against 6,300 kVA installed, so the order holds across the bracket either way. 61% on TX8 and 71% on TX7 at design. %Z SPECIFIED 6.0% +/-10% per IEC 60076, not a nameplate figure: the band is derived from the switchgear, because the NSX incomers are 100 kA and the margin is 1.25, so any impedance below about 5.6% cannot be switched by these devices. At 4-5% the answer is a fuse at the transformer, not a larger frame. Both units within 5% of each other so load divides evenly when either carries both boards. Tap: on-load, +/-3 x 2.5%, delivered mid-position, to commission at +5% - at nominal the far end sits 4.8-6.2% below nominal against a wiring drop of 0.54-1.86%, and +5% brings all 97 circuits inside the limit with the terminals at 100.1-100.8%. ONAN/ONAF, 65/75 K windings, rated at 40 C ambient - a unit quoted at the standard 25 C loses about 3% of its rating in a 40 C switchroom. Buchholz, oil temperature, pressure relief, fan failure alarm, LV neutral to its own terminal, one core bonded per transformer. CONFIRMED: 11 kV, from the MVSB1 main switchboard supplying TX7 and TX8. STILL NOT KNOWN: the transformer's own percent impedance — 6% is assumed, and it is the transformer alone. The 11 kV network is in series with it, so the real fault level at 415 V is LOWER than the 73 kA this design assumes: about 60 kA on a 250 MVA supply, 66 kA on 500 MVA. Every figure in this project is therefore conservative in the safe direction, and the 100 kA incomers carry more margin than quoted. The network's own fault level at MVSB1 is worth asking for, but nothing waits on it. Full specification: docs/transformer-specification.md

panels.notes: Stand-by machine — the schedule describes it as a VSD stand-by and gives it no running load, so it contributes nothing to the board loading. It still draws a full inrush when it starts, so the nameplate rated current has to be recorded at commissioning before the starting current can be checked. On a stand-by that does not start on a supply failure the consequence is a trip rather than a hazard, so this is a commissioning item and not an open question. 500 kW ZR VSD against the 600 A device already fitted.
